note: WIDE funnel for the single 'science' category, restricted to its allowed_domains. Science window = 14 days / 336h (start ~2026-07-17T22:00Z); every item date-verified via og article:published_time / JSON-LD / byline and gated FRESH via `python3 pipeline/freshness.py <iso> 2026-07-31T22:00:41Z science`. Per the rotation plan I emphasized fresher axes (astronomy/ML cosmology, quantum ML+chemistry, materials, climate/geoscience ML, research-automation) and de-emphasized the just-saturated protein/enzyme, genomics, QEC, BCI and battery beats. Outlet diversity is moderate: phys.org (3, at the =3 collection cap), techxplore.com (2), thequantuminsider.com (1), technologyreview.com (1) = 4 distinct outlets; ax-curator later tightens to <=2/outlet. WHY not wider: newscientist.com is blocked to our agent; physics.aps.org 'Quantum Neural Networks Face the Hardware Test' (v19/100, ~Jul 22) returned HTTP 403 (unverifiable -> dropped); space.com 'AI finds 27,000 asteroids' and universetoday 'ML classified half a million galaxies' had no extractable published date (dropped, never guessed). DROPPED as STALE after date-check: eurekalert 1134424 TUD 'LLMs reveal how people make decisions' (Jun 30), genengnews Illumina Billion Cell Atlas (Jan 13), sciencedaily 'AI wrote a paper that passed peer review' (SciAm, Mar 27), MIT News 'Helping AI models meet the real world' (Jul 14, 17d), sciencedaily cancer-paper-mill integrity tool (Jul 16) and superconductor ML (Jul 7). DROPPED per relevance rule: pure AI-industry/business items (pharma AI platform deals, NVIDIA GTC, funding pieces). No social channels defined for science -> none collected.

items.title: AI and quantum chemistry combine to identify efficient blue OLED materials
items.excerpt: Nagoya University researchers paired quantum-chemistry simulation with machine learning to design boron-free molecules that emit vivid, high-color-purity blue light for next-gen OLED displays. Shows ML compressing the search for new functional materials with a real display-tech payoff.

items.title: AI-powered system offers unprecedented insight into the forces shaping Earth's climate
items.excerpt: Tel Aviv University's GOFLOW is an AI system that reconstructs hidden ocean-surface currents directly from satellite imagery, extracting dynamics previously inaccessible. A new ML method that turns existing observations into better climate prediction inputs.

items.title: AI extracts hidden material rules from microscopic data to predict large-scale behavior
items.excerpt: NUS researchers created ML methods that learn large-scale material behavior from microscopic data by discovering hidden variables that capture collective dynamics, cutting computational cost. A methods advance for predicting how materials evolve, relevant to energy and manufacturing.

items.title: How AI helps scientists design the next generation of medicines
items.excerpt: A look at how machine-learning models now enhance every stage of pharmaceutical R&D -- design, make, test, analyze -- compressing timelines and cracking previously intractable discovery problems. Maps how AI is reshaping the day-to-day method and craft of drug research.
